themes.name: Smartphones
themes.description: Advancements in smartphone technology focusing on hardware, performance, user interface, and applications, enhancing modern communication.

linked_companies.name: APPLE INC
linked_companies.description: Designs, manufactures, and markets a globally distributed line of smartphones that integrate proprietary hardware, operating systems, and digital services to drive industry-wide mobile technology adoption.
linked_companies.evidence: Apple's integration within the smartphone industry is driven by its iPhone segment, which generated $57 billion in Q2 2026 to account for over 51% of the company's total quarterly revenue. The recent launch of the iPhone 17 lineup, featuring proprietary A19 chips and integrated AI capabilities, resulted in a 22% year-over-year revenue increase and secured a 99% U.S. customer satisfaction rate. Building upon the previous quarter's record $85.3 billion in smartphone sales, Apple continues to capture market share by maintaining the top-selling device rankings across major global markets including the U.S., Urban China, and Japan.

linked_companies.name: QUALCOMM INC
linked_companies.description: Designs and supplies essential mobile platforms, 5G modems, and radio frequency systems that power the processing and connectivity capabilities of smartphones worldwide.
linked_companies.evidence: Qualcomm's integration with the smartphone industry is anchored by its QCT handset division, an operational core that generates up to 63% of total quarterly revenues, reaching $7.8 billion in peak quarters. The company establishes its market positioning through multi-year agreements, supplying over 70% of the silicon for Samsung's premium models and retaining a 20% design footprint in new Apple phone launches. Furthermore, Qualcomm's engineering investments prioritize the transition to AI-native hardware, utilizing proprietary Snapdragon platforms and specialized mobile processors to drive an anticipated device upgrade cycle centered on agentic smartphones.

linked_companies.name: CIRRUS LOGIC INC
linked_companies.description: Develops low-power, high-precision mixed-signal processing solutions, such as audio codecs and haptic drivers, that enable advanced audio and tactile functionalities in modern smartphones.
linked_companies.evidence: Cirrus Logic anchors its business strategy on the smartphone ecosystem, explicitly dedicating the first two pillars of its long-term growth plan to this market. The company targets its research and development investments toward maintaining its flagship smartphone audio business and increasing high-performance mixed-signal (HPMS) content, producing advanced camera controllers and custom smart power ICs for Face ID 3D sensing implementations. This product pipeline is supported by a two-decade engineering partnership with its largest smartphone customer, which recently accounted for 94% of the revenue mix. Direct demand for these specialized components across both the Audio and HPMS segments serves as the primary driver for the company's $2 billion in annual revenue.

linked_companies.name: QORVO INC
linked_companies.description: Supplies critical radio frequency solutions, including filters and front-end modules, that power cellular connectivity and 5G performance across a wide range of global smartphone platforms.
linked_companies.evidence: Qorvo's engagement with the smartphone industry is anchored by its Advanced Cellular Group, a segment that supplies RF and cellular solutions and accounts for nearly 70% of total company revenue. The company's financial structure within this market is highly concentrated, with its top two global smartphone OEM customers generating approximately 60% of total sales. Operationally, the division functions under dedicated executive leadership and is actively executing a strategic portfolio rotation by reducing R&D product development costs for lower-margin, mass-market Android devices. This resizing, which anticipates a $300 million reduction in mass-tier Android revenue for fiscal 2027, realigns Qorvo's engineering resources to focus exclusively on high-value components for flagship and premium smartphone tiers.

linked_companies.name: SKYWORKS SOLUTIONS INC
linked_companies.description: Develops high-performance radio frequency and mixed-signal semiconductor solutions that enable advanced wireless connectivity and 5G capabilities for major smartphone manufacturers.
linked_companies.evidence: Skyworks' connection to the smartphone industry is driven by its Mobile business segment, which accounted for 58% of total company revenue in Q2 2026. The company recently secured a multigenerational design win with a leading Android OEM, expected to generate over $1 billion in revenue through 2030 by supplying connectivity components for premium AI-enabled devices. To capitalize on shortening AI-capable upgrade cycles and increasing RF complexity, Skyworks assigns dedicated engineering teams to advance multi-year handset projects and defend core device sockets. The vast majority of its mobile revenue is tied to flagship devices, making its overarching financial performance heavily dependent on the strategic demands and market share fluctuations of major smartphone manufacturers.

themes.name: Consumer Electronics
themes.description: Devices and gadgets used daily, such as smartphones, laptops, and home appliances, defining modern lifestyles through innovation in communication, productivity, and entertainment.

linked_companies.name: APPLE INC
linked_companies.description: Designs, manufactures, and markets a comprehensive ecosystem of consumer electronics, including smartphones, personal computers, tablets, and wearable devices, driving global hardware adoption and integration.
linked_companies.evidence: Apple's direct alignment with the consumer electronics industry is defined by its extensive ecosystem of interconnected personal hardware, which recently reached an installed base of over 2.5 billion active devices globally. The company's core product lineup—encompassing the iPhone 17 series, M5-powered Macs, iPads, and daily smart gear like AirPods—generated $80.2 billion in recent quarterly sales, accounting for over 72% of total revenue. This continuous hardware production is sustained by a dedicated engineering division and supported by tens of billions of dollars in active manufacturing obligations and capital expenditures aimed specifically at assembling and delivering finished electronic devices.

linked_companies.name: BEST BUY CO INC
linked_companies.description: Functions as a primary retail channel for a vast array of consumer electronics, providing computing devices, home theater systems, mobile phones, and related tech services to facilitate widespread consumer access to technology.
linked_companies.evidence: Best Buy's foundational business model is anchored entirely in the retailing of technology and consumer electronics, generating nearly $9 billion in quarterly revenue across computing, mobile devices, and home theater systems. Hardware sales, including an explicitly defined 26% "Consumer Electronics" segment, comprise over 80% of the company's overarching revenue profile. The firm leverages its massive physical retail footprint and 80,000-employee workforce to deliver expert in-person curation, driving exclusive vendor partnerships such as securing national launch rights for next-generation RGB television displays. To further support these product ecosystems, Best Buy actively reconfigures its store layouts to feature immersive merchandising spaces for major technology brands.

linked_companies.name: WHIRLPOOL CORP
linked_companies.description: Manufactures and distributes a comprehensive range of major home appliances and electronic devices, integrating connected technologies into everyday household products.
linked_companies.evidence: Whirlpool operates as a pure-play manufacturer within the Consumer Electronics sector, generating over 90% of its revenue from domestic home appliances through dedicated global divisions like Major Domestic Appliances (MDA) and Small Domestic Appliances (SDA). The company solidifies its position as the largest domestic appliance producer by operating an expansive 11-factory U.S. manufacturing footprint—recently expanded with a new $60 million facility in Ohio—while capitalizing on structural tariff advantages. To sustain this manufacturing dominance and expand its appliance portfolio, Whirlpool is executing a $400 million capital expenditure plan focused on digital transformation and product innovation, funding the development of advanced consumer devices such as intelligent wall ovens and proprietary UV laundry towers.

linked_companies.name: SHARKNINJA INC
linked_companies.description: Designs and manufactures a broad portfolio of consumer electronics and small household appliances aimed at enhancing everyday living through innovative home technology.
linked_companies.evidence: SharkNinja operates entirely within the consumer electronics space, generating its $1.41 billion in first-quarter net sales exclusively from technologically advanced home gadgets and appliances. The company's core strategy revolves around conceptualizing and manufacturing lifestyle electronics across 39 subcategories, including vacuum cleaners, smart beauty tools, and personal cooling systems like the proprietary Shark ChillPill. To power this disruptive product pipeline, SharkNinja allocates its projected $190 million to $210 million capital expenditure budget and $99 million in quarterly research and development spending directly toward driving home appliance innovations. Furthermore, the company leverages a dedicated workforce of over 4,000 employees specifically focused on designing, engineering, and expanding this consumer electronics portfolio.

linked_companies.name: UNIVERSAL DISPLAY CORP
linked_companies.description: Supplies proprietary organic light-emitting diode (OLED) technologies and materials that enable the production of advanced, power-efficient displays for smartphones, televisions, smartwatches, and other consumer electronic devices.
linked_companies.evidence: Universal Display Corporation functions as a foundational supplier to the consumer electronics value chain by providing the essential emissive materials that power billions of devices, including televisions, smartphones, and foldables. Backed by a portfolio of over 7,000 global patents, the company's proprietary OLED technologies are deeply integrated across major consumer categories like wearables, tablets, laptops, and monitors. Because this sector serves as the exclusive end-market for its commercialized materials, recent macro pressures and limited visibility across the consumer electronics ecosystem directly prompted the company to revise its near-term financial guidance.

themes.name: 5G Infrastructure
themes.description: Network technologies enabling high-speed mobile connectivity and increased bandwidth, supporting modern communication demands and emerging technologies like IoT and AI.

linked_companies.name: CROWN CASTLE INC
linked_companies.description: Provides essential shared communications infrastructure, including a vast network of macro towers, small cells, and fiber optics, that enables wireless carriers to deploy, densify, and scale 5G networks.
linked_companies.evidence: Crown Castle operates a stand-alone tower business that generates $3.9 billion in site rental revenues by serving as the foundational physical infrastructure for mobile network 5G rollouts. The company directly enables ongoing carrier network densification by providing critical site space for colocation, additional radios, and high-speed spectrum installations. Positioning its portfolio with a specific skew toward urban and suburban environments allows the company to capture early-cycle demand from major telecom tenants deploying next-generation networks. Additionally, the company continuously funds capital improvements to structurally modify its towers, ensuring they can physically host advanced active 5G equipment such as massive MIMO antennas throughout the multi-year deployment cycle.

linked_companies.name: QUALCOMM INC
linked_companies.description: Designs and supplies foundational wireless technologies, advanced modem-RF systems, and specialized radio access network platforms that enable the global deployment and operation of 5G network infrastructure.
linked_companies.evidence: Qualcomm's engagement with 5G infrastructure stems from its foundational role in standardizing, manufacturing, and licensing cellular connectivity technologies across its primary business units. The company's QCT segment revenues rely heavily on the production of 5G sub-6 and 5G millimeter wave radio frequency front-end (RFFE) components, alongside its 5G-enabled Snapdragon platforms. Furthermore, Qualcomm leverages extensive intellectual property within its QTL licensing division to support global deployments of 5G fixed wireless solutions and AI-powered Radio Access Networks. Sustained research and development investments continue to integrate these 5G cellular capabilities with on-device AI to drive hardware adoption throughout the broader mobile and IoT ecosystems.

linked_companies.name: AMERICAN TOWER CORP
linked_companies.description: Provides essential multitenant communications real estate and macro tower sites globally, enabling major wireless carriers to deploy, densify, and expand their 5G networks.
linked_companies.evidence: American Tower acts as the physical structural foundation for 5G networks by providing the macro towers necessary for global carrier antenna deployments. Driven by increasing mobile data consumption and ongoing 5G adoption, network densification efforts currently support approximately 4% organic tenant billings growth across the company's portfolio. To facilitate this capacity-oriented activity and the continued deployment of limited-propagation, high-band spectrums, the company is allocating the majority of its $1.9 billion capital budget to construct roughly 2,000 new sites worldwide. These infrastructure investments directly enable telecom operators in the U.S., Europe, and emerging markets to expand their physical footprint and meet compounding 5G connectivity demands.

linked_companies.name: T-MOBILE US INC
linked_companies.description: Deploys and operates a nationwide 5G network, leveraging broad spectrum assets and advanced wireless infrastructure to deliver high-speed connectivity for consumer and enterprise applications.
linked_companies.evidence: T-Mobile positions its nationwide 5G advanced network as the foundational asset driving its $77 billion service revenue base, customer acquisitions, and fixed wireless broadband expansion. Claiming a multiyear competitive advantage, the company emphasizes it is the sole carrier to roll out 5G Advanced nationwide, utilizing unique technological features like uplink transmit switching and uplink MIMO to connect physical AI, humanoid robots, and edge computing. To sustain this technological lead, T-Mobile directs its $10 billion capital expenditure budget heavily toward continuous network build-outs, dedicating billions in quarterly cash purchases toward property, equipment, and strategic 600 MHz and 800 MHz spectrum licenses. This physical infrastructure deployment is scaled through thousands of greenfield site builds and the multibillion-dollar integration of UScellular's wireless operations to enhance rural coverage and deliver advanced capabilities like network slicing.

linked_companies.name: SBA COMMUNICATIONS CORP
linked_companies.description: Owns and operates multi-tenant wireless communications infrastructure, leasing essential tower and antenna space to telecommunications carriers to support the deployment, densification, and expansion of 5G networks.
linked_companies.evidence: SBA Communications provides the underlying physical tower infrastructure carriers require to expand 5G networks utilizing new spectrums like C-band. The company's domestic and international leasing activity is driven by demand for new colocations and site amendments designed to host modernized network architectures, including massive MIMO antennas and high-frequency radios. Additionally, through widespread master lease agreements, such as a ten-year modernization partnership with Verizon, SBA's digital real estate structurally accommodates growing network densification needs and high-capacity use cases like fixed wireless access.

themes.name: Internet Of Things
themes.description: Interconnected network of physical devices embedded with sensors and software, enabling data collection and exchange for improved automation and analytics.

linked_companies.name: SILICON LABORATORIES INC
linked_companies.description: Develops specialized wireless microcontrollers, sensors, and software platforms that provide secure connectivity and enable the deployment of Internet of Things devices across smart home, commercial, and industrial applications.
linked_companies.evidence: SLAB's product portfolio of analog-intensive, mixed-signal solutions is exclusively engineered for Internet of Things (IoT) applications, generating the entirety of the company's $213.5 million revenue in Q2 2026 across its Industrial & Commercial and Home & Life segments. To advance this central technology theme, the company directed $88.6 million—accounting for 41.5% of its quarterly revenue—into research and development for its integrated hardware and software platforms. This focused investment sustains the firm's position as a provider of secure, intelligent wireless technology, underpinned by an intellectual property moat where U.S. patents cover substantially all of its IoT products.

linked_companies.name: SAMSARA INC-CL A
linked_companies.description: Delivers a comprehensive Connected Operations Cloud that integrates Internet of Things devices, including telematics and video sensors, to digitize, monitor, and optimize physical assets and fleets across industrial sectors.
linked_companies.evidence: Samsara's operations rely on the Internet of Things, with approximately 98% of its revenue generated from subscriptions to its Connected Operations Platform, a system that consolidates data directly from proprietary IoT devices. The company instruments physical assets using interconnected hardware—such as wireless gateways, multicam sensors, and Asset Tags—to construct a large, defensible data asset. Reflecting the interdependence of its software platform and physical hardware, Samsara actively expands its IoT infrastructure through a $97.5 million quarterly research and development budget and aggressive headcount additions across its sales and customer support teams. Ongoing financial commitments toward cellular connectivity and increased connected device costs reinforce IoT hardware as the foundational layer of the company's enterprise ecosystem.

linked_companies.name: ALARM.COM HOLDINGS INC
linked_companies.description: Provides a cloud-based platform for intelligently connected properties, integrating a vast network of smart sensors, security systems, and automation devices to enable seamless remote monitoring and control within the Internet of Things ecosystem.
linked_companies.evidence: Alarm.com’s foundational business model is built entirely on the Internet of Things, orchestrating connected physical devices across residential, commercial, and utility sectors to drive its global SaaS and hardware revenue. The company allocates substantial resources to this architecture by deploying a 1,140-person R&D workforce dedicated to IoT coordination and operating EnergyHub, a distinct division delivering mission-critical distributed IoT management solutions. This structural reliance on IoT ecosystems drives high subscriber retention and establishes a massive scale advantage, reinforced by a platform that manages over 170 million connected devices generating hundreds of billions of data points.

linked_companies.name: SEMTECH CORP
linked_companies.description: Develops foundational wireless connectivity solutions, including proprietary LoRa technology and cellular modules, enabling low-power, wide-area networks for diverse Internet of Things applications across industrial and commercial sectors.
linked_companies.evidence: Semtech Corporation's engagement with the Internet of Things is driven by its dedicated 'IoT Systems and Connectivity' operating segment, which combines with its proprietary LoRa wireless platform to generate nearly half of the company's total revenue. The company designs and markets a comprehensive portfolio of networking hardware—including modules, gateways, and routers—powered by its fourth-generation LoRa technology, which currently connects over 150 million end nodes across smart utilities, smart buildings, and Amazon Sidewalk ecosystems. To sustain this focus, management directs a core portion of its enterprise R&D budget and active hiring programs toward expanding multiprotocol IoT architectures, building upon strategic integrations like the Sierra Wireless acquisition.

linked_companies.name: DIGI INTERNATIONAL INC
linked_companies.description: Provides business and mission-critical Internet of Things connectivity products, software, and services that enable secure communication and remote management of distributed device networks.
linked_companies.evidence: Digi International operates as a pure-play provider in the industrial Internet of Things (IoT) market, delivering comprehensive end-to-end solutions spanning edge hardware, software, and connectivity for remote asset management. The company's organizational framework is entirely dedicated to this market, generating 100 percent of its $157 million Annualized Recurring Revenue exclusively through its "IoT Products & Services" and "IoT Solutions" reporting segments. Capital allocation and workforce integration align strictly with this operational identity, highlighted by the strategic acquisitions of Particle and Jolt. These purchases incorporated specialized teams into Digi's dedicated SmartSense division, contributing over $20 million in new recurring revenue and integrating an ecosystem of 240,000 developers into the company's industrial IoT portfolio.

themes.name: Streaming Platforms & Services
themes.description: Platforms offering media content directly to consumers over the internet, enabling on-demand access and convenient delivery of films, series, music, and other entertainment.

linked_companies.name: NETFLIX INC
linked_companies.description: Operates a global subscription-based entertainment platform that delivers a diverse library of original and licensed films, television series, and games directly to consumers across internet-connected devices.
linked_companies.evidence: Netflix operates as a pure-play streaming platform, generating its revenue almost entirely from subscriptions and advertising across a global user base of 325 million paid members. Directed by its executive leadership team, the company centers its strategic and capital allocation framework on enhancing its media delivery infrastructure, allocating nearly a billion dollars in quarterly technology and development spending. To maximize engagement across an addressable market of 800 million smart TV households, the platform is expanding its core offerings into multi-format entertainment, recently drawing 31.4 million viewers for live programming such as the World Baseball Classic. The company's fundamental reliance on the streaming sector is further evidenced by major strategic maneuvers, including its recent multi-billion dollar pursuit of Warner Bros. Discovery's direct-to-consumer assets to expand its studio and content portfolio.

linked_companies.name: ROKU INC
linked_companies.description: Operates a comprehensive television streaming platform that connects users to digital content through proprietary operating systems, streaming players, and smart TVs, while driving monetization through advertising, premium subscriptions, and content distribution.
linked_companies.evidence: Roku functions as a central distribution ecosystem in the Streaming Platforms & Services industry, recently surpassing 100 million streaming households globally and facilitating nearly half of all streaming time in U.S. broadband households. The company monetizes this vast scale through its Platform segment—which generated 91% of total net revenue in recent quarters—by distributing third-party apps and expanding owned-and-operated services such as The Roku Channel, the ad-free subscription service Howdy, and the recently acquired Frndly TV. To maintain this infrastructure, the company utilizes a dedicated Roku Media division led by a President-level executive and directs its engineering headcount and R&D efforts toward enhancing its proprietary Roku TV OS and deploying major home screen updates.

linked_companies.name: SPOTIFY TECHNOLOGY SA
linked_companies.description: Provides a global digital audio streaming platform that delivers music, podcasts, and audiobooks to users through ad-supported and premium subscription models, driving engagement via personalized content discovery.
linked_companies.evidence: Spotify operates as a direct-to-consumer internet media streaming platform, generating its EUR 4.5 billion in recent quarterly revenue entirely from premium subscriptions and ad-supported tiers. The system delivers on-demand digital content, including music, podcasts, audiobooks, and newly added fitness videos, to 761 million monthly active users and 293 million subscribers. The company's organizational structure and capital strategy are dedicated to maintaining and expanding this ecosystem, demonstrated by continuous technological reinvestments and an $11 billion payout to content rights holders.

linked_companies.name: WALT DISNEY CO/THE
linked_companies.description: Operates direct-to-consumer streaming platforms that distribute a comprehensive library of original programming, legacy media franchises, and live sports broadcasts to a global subscriber base.
linked_companies.evidence: Disney positions streaming platforms at the core of its operational strategy, explicitly targeting the evolution of Disney+ into the interactive digital centerpiece of the enterprise. Supported by the dedicated Disney Entertainment DTC unit, specialized technology teams are aggressively iterating product enhancements, including a fully integrated Hulu experience designed to reduce subscriber churn. These ecosystem improvements, combined with global content scaling and targeted bundling strategies, have accelerated sequential SVOD revenue growth to 13% and propelled streaming revenues to more than double those of traditional linear networks. Furthermore, following a corporate restructuring to ensure executive bottom-line accountability, these multi-billion dollar capital investments have successfully transitioned the streaming segment into a highly profitable division characterized by double-digit financial margins.

linked_companies.name: FUBOTV INC -CLASS A
linked_companies.description: Operates a sports-first live TV streaming platform that delivers a comprehensive mix of premium sports, news, and entertainment content to subscribers across various digital devices.
linked_companies.evidence: Fubo operates exclusively as a pure-play direct-to-consumer live TV streaming provider, maintaining its Fubo and Hulu Live brands as its sole operating segment. Following a business combination with Hulu + Live TV, the company established itself as the second-largest virtual multichannel video programming distributor (vMVPD) in the United States with 6.2 million North American subscribers. These platforms define the entirety of the company's business model, accounting for 100% of its $1.68 billion pro forma quarterly revenue in early 2026 and guiding ongoing technology investments to unify its global streaming architecture.
